source_ref: OSF dqw9f (public node; API reports no node licence): Studies In Main Text/Study 2 Data and Code/Study 2 Data no ID.sav (https://osf.io/download/hymb6/, sha256 390e7966...65b27f), Supplemental Studies/Study S1c Data and Code/Study S1c Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/2knxu/, sha256 4a5debaf...d9142e) and Supplemental Studies/Study S2c Data and Code/Study S2c Data.sav (https://osf.io/download/6501f901f3dcd16832ddd406/, sha256 77e72d25...e4732e) -- SPSS variable and value labels of belong1-5; data/wallace_2026_mindsets.py for the code derivation and the S2c recode. Paper: Wallace, Murphy, Hernandez-Colmenares & Fujita (2026) JPSP 130(2) 291-307, doi:10.1037/pspi0000498.
note: Level 1, both label levels read. Code derivation: item IS the source column name (belong1/2/3/4R/5 in S1c and S2c), plus one mechanical rename in Study 2, whose column is belong4 and which the script writes as belong4R; its label is the same 'alienated' item, so exempt from Step 5b and no verification files. PER-STUDY VARIANTS: live cov_study 1 = Study 2 (838 ids), 4 = S1c (796), 7 = S2c (793). S1c and S2c labels are character-identical ('...in this organization?'); Study 2's refer to a class/professor ('...during class with this professor?', '...during this class?'). Following the batch_644 convention, item_text carries both verbatim labels prefixed 'Study 2 (cov_study = 1): ' / 'Studies S1c and S2c (cov_study = 4, 7): ' and joined by ' | '; prefixes and separator are IRW's, wording after each prefix is the label verbatim, including curly quotes and the source's double space in belong5 ('“fit in”  in this organization'). OPTIONS: Study 2 and S1c value labels are 1='1 - not at all' ... 7='7 - extremely'; S2c's run the other way (1='1 - extremely' ... 7='7 - not at all') and the script rewrote S2c as 8-resp (itemcov_recoded=1 on all 3965 S2c rows). Route 9 against the cached live table: all 15 study x item count vectors match cell for cell, e.g. S1c belong1 29/49/50/96/194/219/159 source = live; Study 2 belong4(R) 115/151/146/127/138/83/78 = live; S2c belong1 source 120/188/164/133/91/50/47 -> live 47/50/91/133/164/188/120 (exact reversal). S2c direction cross-checked: raw S2c belong1 correlates +0.82 with S2c fit1 (1 = Strongly agree), so its printed 1 = extremely labels are correct and the recode is right. So resp 1 = not at all, 7 = extremely in every study; option_text ships those two anchors with the source's '1 - '/'7 - ' prefixes stripped; resp 2-6 carry only their own digit in the source and are left blank. belong4R is stored RAW, not reversed despite the R: 'How alienated...' correlates -0.41 to -0.74 with the other four in every study and its mean is 3.29-3.70 against 4.0-5.1 (itemcov_reverse_keyed=1 marks it). No instructions text in any .sav or in the Study 2 .sps; left blank. Rights: study-authored items, no stated restriction located (silence = permission).
public_note: The items were worded differently in the pooled studies (about a class with a professor in Study 2, cov_study = 1; about an organization in Studies S1c and S2c, cov_study = 4 and 7), so item_text gives both wordings labelled by study; responses are coded 1 = not at all to 7 = extremely in all studies, Study S2c having been reverse-recoded from its printed order (itemcov_recoded = 1), and belong4R ('alienated') is not reverse-scored.
